clue.text: Wedding tackle on a horse discussed

indicators.note: something discussed is talked about, so we want the word as it is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a bridle is the headgear and reins used to control a horse

explanation.surface: A rider tacks up a horse for a country wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wedding tackle' looks like a cheeky phrase, but 'Wedding' stands alone as the definition and the horse gear supplies the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridal is the adjective for things belonging to a bride or her marriage ceremony, as in bridal party.

clue.text: Dance is almost pathetic after drink

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is dropped
after places the clipped word behind the drink in the answer

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a drink
bad as in pathetically poor

explanation.surface: Someone's dancing after a few drinks is nearly hopeless.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance with rhythmic hip movements, one example of a dance.

parts.note: DIs are detective inspectors
a face is a side, as of a cube

indicators.note: with its contents removed only the outer letters of the word remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of nastiest

explanation.surface: Police officers confront a vicious, disgruntled troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face' looks like a verb for confronting, but it supplies a noun. DI is the British police rank of detective inspector.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissident openly opposes official policy, a rebel or agitator stirring up dissent.

indicators.note: introduces puts the first piece in front, leading in to the next

parts.note: a band or stripe is a line
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A musical group unveils fresh songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' and 'material' suggest a group with new songs; it is a stripe and cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Linen is cloth woven from flax, so it is an example of a fabric or material.

clue.text: Dog publicity held by Crufts, say

indicators.note: something held by another is gripped inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: Crufts is a famous British dog show, an example of a show
an ad is a piece of publicity

explanation.surface: A dog gets plenty of attention at the Crufts show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' reads as a noun fitting the Crufts scene, but it is the verb meaning to follow closely. Crufts is the big annual dog show held in Birmingham.
explanation.definitionFit: To shadow someone is to follow them closely and persistently, which is exactly what dogging them means.

indicators.note: in a down clue on means sitting above, so the first piece comes earlier

parts.note: a string is a line or cord
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A hard-line stance on how a hospital department is run.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringent rules are strict and exacting, which is what an uncompromising approach demands.

clue.text: Female in a club showing behind

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the following word

parts.note: a bat is a club used in sport
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A woman at a nightclub shows off her rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' and 'behind' suggest a nightclub and a bottom; it is a bat and a nautical position.
explanation.definitionFit: Abaft is a nautical term meaning towards or at the stern, that is, behind on a ship.

clue.text: Single US soldier wearing fancy issue

indicators.note: something wearing clothes is inside them, so these letters go within the next word

parts.note: ornate means fancy, elaborately decorated
I is the Roman numeral one, a single
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A lone American soldier dressed in flashy issue kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' suggests army kit, but it is the verb meaning to emerge from a source.
explanation.definitionFit: To originate is to arise or spring from a source, as to issue from somewhere does.

indicators.note: not starting means losing the opening letter of the word

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
sent as in directed somewhere

explanation.surface: A taxi refuses to start, so the passenger is pointed elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Won't start' sounds like a dead engine but means dropping the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Absent means not present, the same as being away from a place.

indicators.note: to house means to contain within, so the letters sit inside the preceding words

parts.note: found straddling these two words

explanation.surface: Some councillors agreed to provide homes for the needy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' looks like a noun for the needy; it is an adjective for scanty.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means lacking in quantity or quality, so a poor helping is a meagre one.

indicators.note: comprising here means including within it, so the outer word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: bum is informal British for the backside, plus the S of the possessive
p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft

explanation.surface: A cheeky description of a backside's soft curves.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'Bottom's' counts as a letter; the soft P goes inside before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumps are swellings or protrusions on a surface, a plain synonym for small rounded bulges.

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the following word

parts.note: a naive view is an unrealistic one
R is the abbreviation for Republican
a rat is a scoundrel or betrayer

explanation.surface: A political tale casts a Republican as the villain of an implausible yarn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unrealistic' looks like a description of the story, but it is the container that wraps the political pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative is an account of connected events, which is what a story is.

clue.text: I've a son involved in subterfuge

indicators.note: involved suggests something tangled up, so these letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these three words, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A parent confesses that their boy is mixed up in some trickery.
explanation.definitionFit: Evasion is dodging the truth or an obligation by trickery, which is what subterfuge describes.

clue.text: Watching with husband caught in zip

indicators.note: something caught in another is trapped inside it, so one letter goes into the other word

parts.note: noting is observing or watching
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Someone watches as a husband gets caught in his trouser zip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Zip' suggests a fastener, but it is slang for zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Zip is informal, chiefly American, slang for zero or nothing at all, as in 'they won zip'.

clue.text: Persuade sweetheart taking time is fair

indicators.note: taking means holding something within, so one word swallows the other

parts.note: to tempt is to entice or persuade
an era is a period of time
the heart, or middle letter, of the word sweet

explanation.surface: Courting a sweetheart patiently, taking one's time, is only fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' is not a lover but the central letter of 'sweet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperate weather is mild and moderate, so a temperate day is a fair one.

indicators.note: in a down clue a support is underneath, so the worker comes last
revolting means rising up and overturning order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder
an ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: A villainous employee backs disgusting offences.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscreant is a wrongdoer or scoundrel, which is what a rogue is.

clue.text: Sailor fed crew before temperature drop

indicators.note: before places the crew pieces ahead of the final letter

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
fed as in ate a meal
the crew are the men of a ship
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A sailor feeds the crew before the cold sets in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed' looks like a verb acting on the crew but stands alone as ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An abatement is a lessening or reduction in amount or intensity, that is, a drop.

clue.text: Quiet beer, source of gas possibly

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A quiet pint of beer, with a joke about it causing wind.
explanation.walkthrough: The gas is not wind from beer but natural gas extracted by fracking.
explanation.definitionFit: Shale is a sedimentary rock from which natural gas can be extracted, as in shale gas fracking.

indicators.note: something that carries another holds it within, so these letters enclose the other piece

parts.note: a section is a department of an organisation
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A store department stocks a French product line.
explanation.definitionFit: A selection is an assortment of goods to choose from, the same as a range of products.

clue.text: Put out statement, implicitly true initially

definitions.text: Put out statement, implicitly true initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the preceding words

parts.note: the first letters of these five words

explanation.surface: Someone issues a claim that they assume holds good.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: it defines the word and also spells it out with its initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward a proposition as a basis for argument, taking it as true without proof.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an adverb meaning fairly or rather
second meaning: an adjective meaning attractive

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a lukewarm verdict, 'quite nice', but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb the word means fairly, as in 'fairly good'; as an adjective it means attractive or pleasing to look at.

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the following word

parts.note: an artery is a major road, a main traffic route
feeling run-down means being unwell

explanation.surface: A car's flat battery leaves a driver stranded on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battery' suggests a car part, but a battery is also a unit of guns.
explanation.definitionFit: In the army a battery is a unit of big guns, so it is an example of the heavy weapons branch.

parts.note: a yank is a sudden jerk

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, every other one

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of cedes

explanation.surface: An American idiot gives ground time and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' looks like an insult for a person but is a sudden pull.
explanation.definitionFit: Yankee is an informal name, used chiefly by outsiders, for a person from the United States.

indicators.note: some means only part of the words that follow, so the letters lie inside them

parts.note: found straddling these three words

explanation.surface: Someone worries that a pain in the chest might be serious.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is by example: the pain is in the ear, not the chest.
explanation.definitionFit: Earache is a specific kind of pain felt in the ear, so it is one example of a pain.

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above, so the first piece comes earlier

parts.note: to cast is to throw
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A call to overthrow the English class system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw over' reads as overthrow, but 'over' just stacks the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Caste is a rigid hereditary division of society, notably in India, a class system.

parts.note: an uncle is a family relative

indicators.note: oddly tells us to keep the letters in the odd-numbered positions of the word

parts.note: the first and third letters of aunt

explanation.surface: A family visit where an uncle and aunt behave strangely and look grubby.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclean means soiled or impure, the same condition as dirty.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an adjective for complete or absolute
second meaning: a verb for saying out loud

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like praise for a singer's clear tone, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means complete, as in sheer nonsense; as a verb it means to speak or express words.

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the following word

parts.note: Erse is an old name for Scottish or Irish Gaelic
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An editor strikes out a piece written in Gaelic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a news piece but is the grammatical word a.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to rub out or delete, so it means to cancel something.

clue.text: Fleeting time passed one in shot

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the following word

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
ran as in time ran or passed by
shot as in sent flying, propelled
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Time slipped by as one person had a quick go at a shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Transient describes something lasting only a short while, which is what fleeting means.

indicators.note: a filling sits inside something, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for that is (id est)
nan is a flatbread from South Asian cooking

explanation.surface: A complaint about a sandwich whose bread has no filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' sounds like a hollow sandwich but means empty-headed.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly and lacking sense or substance, empty in the sense of vacuous remarks.

clue.text: Witness in terrible state facing time

indicators.note: facing means standing in front of, so the shuffled letters come before the next piece
terrible suggests a mess, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: the anagram fodder
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A shaken witness in a terrible state faces a long prison sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Facing time' sounds like a prison term; here it simply puts T after the shuffled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To witness a document is to sign confirming it is genuine, which is to attest it.

clue.text: About right checking finish for plaster

indicators.note: checking means holding back or restraining, so these letters hold the other piece inside them

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for about or concerning
R is the abbreviation for right
an end is a finish

explanation.surface: A builder checking the right way to finish a plastered wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plaster' sounds like a noun but is a verb here: the coating applied to an outside wall.
explanation.definitionFit: To render a wall is to coat it with a layer of plaster or cement, a building-trade sense.
